extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, securities lawyers, and corporate compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Federal SEC final rules and interpretive guidance on disclosure obligations for registrants regarding climate-related matters (where to disclose, materiality qualifiers, scope including value chain/transition risks, and related Reg S-K/S-X/MD&A requirements). Intended to guide what climate and related environmental information public companies must include in SEC filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy of full disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental purpose of the securities laws is substituting 'a philosophy of full disclosure for the philosophy of caveat emptor.' (quoting Supreme Court and legislative history).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange Act was designed to protect investors against manipulation of stock prices and to implement a philosophy of full disclosure; issuers must make a full and fair disclosure of information relevant to a public offering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management's Discussion and Analysis (Item 303) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 303 of Regulation S-K requires a registrant to discuss its financial condition, changes in its financial condition, and results of operations, and to 'provide such other information that the registrant believes to be necessary to an understanding of its financial condition, changes in financial condition, and results of operation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission guidance states investors should understand the extent to which accounting changes and changes in business activity have affected comparability of year-to-year data and be able to assess the source and probability of recurrence of net income (or loss). See Concept Release on MD&A and prior Guidelines for Registration and Reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of climate-related disclosure in filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate change disclosure might, depending on the circumstances, be required in a company's Description of Business, Risk Factors, Legal Proceedings, and MD&A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2010 Guidance identified certain climate-related issues companies may need to consider and stated registrants should consider any financial statement implications of climate change issues in accordance with applicable accounting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of material pending legal proceedings (17 CFR 229.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: 17 CFR 229.103 requires a registrant to describe its material pending legal proceedings, other than ordinary routine litigation incidental to the business, and indicates that administrative or judicial proceedings arising under Federal, state, or local law regulating the discharge of materials into the environment shall not be deemed 'ordinary routine litigation incidental to the business' and must be described if meeting certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically, Form A-1 required certain information related to legal proceedings (origin, nature, names of parties). The 1982 Release moved and codified the requirement to disclose material pending legal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of material effects of environmental regulation (17 CFR 229.101(c)(2)(i) / 229.101(c)(1)(xii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate disclosure shall be made as to the material effects that compliance with Federal, State and local provisions regulating the discharge of materials into the environment, or otherwise relating to the protection of the environment, may have upon the capital expenditures, earnings and competitive position of the registrant and its subsidiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 1982 Release moved the requirement to disclose information regarding the material effects of compliance with environmental provisions, and also the disclosure of material estimated capital expenditures for environmental control facilities to 17 CFR 229.101(c)(1)(xii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate-related disclosures under subpart 1500 (17 CFR 229.1500 / 1502)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart 1500 of Regulation S-K and 17 CFR 229.1502(a) set out disclosure requirements addressing climate-related risks; registrants must disclose climate-related information where material under the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules are intended to be consistent with other disclosure items and to require disclosure of climate-related risks appropriate for investor decision-making, even where other regimes substantively regulate those issues. See definitions and specific subpart provisions for scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality qualification for transition risk in value chain
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant would only need to disclose the transition risk of a party in its value chain when such transition risk has materially impacted or is reasonably likely to materially impact the registrant itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: transition risk from the Inflation Reduction Act could materially impact a registrant that produces or uses less energy efficient products, affecting its business, results of operations, or financial condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality qualifiers to limit detailed climate disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules add materiality qualifiers to certain climate risk disclosure requirements so that detailed disclosure is elicited only when it is material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses concerns that highly prescriptive disclosure requirements could produce excessive information not decision-useful to most investors; materiality qualifiers narrow the obligation to material items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart 1500 excludes non-climate weather events
rubrics_metrics.description: Although Article 14 of Regulation S-X requires disclosure of certain financial effects of severe weather events and other natural conditions, subpart 1500 of Regulation S-K does not require the disclosure of material impacts from non-climate-related weather events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission explains the distinction between weather (short-term changes) and climate (long-term conditions) consistent with NOAA definitions; registrants need only disclose climate-related impacts under subpart 1500.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose methodologies and data sources for flood disclosure (commenter recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If address-specific locations are not required, the Commission should require the disclosure of methodologies and data sources used for flooding disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This recommendation (e.g., from Wellington Management) aims to preserve decision-useful information when more granular, address-level disclosure is not mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to TCFD guidance on metrics, targets, and transition plans
rubrics_metrics.description: The release references TCFD Guidance on Metrics, Targets, and Transition Plans (section E) as relevant guidance for metrics and targets disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants and commenters pointed to TCFD documents as authoritative guidance for the design and presentation of climate-related metrics, targets, and transition plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of accounting policies and market-risk information (17 CFR 229.305)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation S-K requires disclosure of accounting policies for derivative financial instruments and quantitative and qualitative information about market risk inherent in derivative financial instruments and other financial instruments (17 CFR 229.305).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These disclosure items historically addressed market-risk and derivatives and can intersect with climate-related disclosures where climate risks affect financial instruments or market risk profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on summarizing risk factors for speculative offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior guidance (Guide 6, 1968) recommended that, if the securities to be offered are of a highly speculative nature, the registrant should provide 'a carefully organized series of short, concise paragraphs summarizing the principal factors that make the offering speculative.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This historical guidance demonstrates the Commission's long-standing expectation that risk factors be presented in a concise, organized manner that highlights principal risks to investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of leased assets and rental commitments (Regulation S-X Rule 3-16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to Rule 3-16 of Regulation S-X required disclosure of, among other things, total rental expenses and minimum rental commitments to enable investors to determine the nature and magnitude of such assets and the impact upon net income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission adopted improved disclosures of leases because prior corporate disclosure of leased assets 'has not been sufficient' for investor understanding; analogous intent underlies climate-related financial disclosure improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statements include notes and related schedules (Schedule A / 17 CFR 210.1-01(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'form' required by the Commission includes both financial statements and notes to those statements; 17 CFR 210.1-01(b) specifies that the term 'financial statements' includes all notes to the statements and related schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Climate-related financial effects may need to be reflected in financial statements and the accompanying notes/schedules consistent with applicable accounting standards and Schedule A requirements.
